name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle or tricycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Class 1 and Class 3 assist only while the rider pedals, cutting out at 20 and 28 mph; Class 2 may be propelled by the motor alone, to 20 mph

One whose motor is 750 W or more, or that fits none of the three classes, isn't an electric bicycle: with pedals, a motor of 1.5 brake horsepower (1,125 W) or less and a top speed of 25 mph it is a moped, needing a driver license, registration and insurance; otherwise it is a motor driven cycle up to 5 horsepower (3,750 W) and a motorcycle past it, both needing a class M license, title, registration and insurance
May have two or three wheels
Carries a permanent label, in at least 9-point type, stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Has the rights and duties of a bicycle, except where a local authority regulates it otherwise
Not a vehicle or motor vehicle under Arizona law, and excluded from the moped, motorcycle and motor driven cycle definitions
No title, registration, vehicle license tax, driver's license or insurance
No statewide minimum age or helmet requirement; cities may set their own
Class 1 and Class 2 may ride bicycle and multi-use paths, but the local authority or state agency over a path may ban them
Class 3 is kept off bicycle and multi-use paths unless the path runs within or beside a road or the agency over it allows it
